title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Veterinary Medicine (2015)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Veterinary Medicine (2015). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: One of the following is common characteristics of Fasciola and Schistosoma.
questions.explanation:
Both Fasciola (liver fluke) and Schistosoma (blood fluke) require snail intermediate hosts in their life cycles.
Fasciola is hermaphroditic while Schistosoma has separate sexes (option a incorrect).
Only Fasciola's infective stage is metacercaria (option b incorrect).
While Fasciola affects the liver, Schistosoma primarily affects blood vessels (option d partially incorrect).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a cause of environmental mastitis?
questions.explanation:
Staphylococcus aureus is primarily a contagious mastitis pathogen transmitted during milking.
The other three (Klebsiella, E. coli, S. uberis) are environmental pathogens acquired between milkings from the cow's environment.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a common cause of constipation?
options: Diseases of the fore-stomach and abomasum causing failure of outflow
questions.explanation:
Partial obstruction of the small intestine typically causes diarrhea (not constipation) due to increased fluid secretion.
The other options are well-established causes of constipation in animals.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is false?
options: Biological vector is a vector in which an infectious agent undergoes either a necessary part of its lifecycle or multiplication, before transmission to the natural or secondary host
The continued survival of the infectious agents depends on their successful transmission to susceptible host
Horizontal transmission is the transmission of a disease agent among contemporaries from one animal to the other within same generation
vector is a vertebrate animal, usually an arthropod that transmits infectious agents between vertebrate animals
questions.explanation:
Vectors are typically invertebrates (arthropods), not vertebrate animals.
All other statements are correct definitions in epidemiology.

questions.questionText: Identify the one which is incorrect about eradication of disease?
options: It is reduction of infectious disease prevalence to a level at which it will not worry of the community
It is extinctions of an infectious agent till a single agent could survive on earth
It is reduction of infectious disease prevalence to a level at which transmission does not occur
questions.explanation:
Eradication means complete permanent reduction to zero cases worldwide (not just reducing to a non-worrying level).
Option a describes control, not eradication.

questions.questionText: If the prevalence is low as compared to the incidence of the disease, it implies;
options: Nothing can be said because they are separate entities.
The disease is either very fatal or easily curable.
questions.explanation:
Low prevalence relative to incidence suggests either:
1) High fatality (cases don't survive long to contribute to prevalence), or
2) Rapid cure/short duration (cases resolve quickly).

questions.questionText: Which of the following metacestode stages represents beef measles?
questions.explanation:
Cysticercus bovis is the larval stage of Taenia saginata in cattle ('beef measles').
C. cellulose (pork measles), C. ovis (sheep), and C. tendullis are other metacestodes.

questions.questionText: A cohort study differs from a case-control study in that:
options: Subjects are enrolled or categorized on the basis of their exposure status in a cohort study but not in a case-control study
Cohort studies require many years to conduct, but case-control studies do not
Subjects are asked about their exposure status in a cohort study but not in a case-control study
Cohort studies are conducted to investigate chronic diseases, case-control studies are used for infectious diseases
questions.explanation:
Key difference:
Cohort: Start with exposure → follow for outcome
Case-control: Start with outcome → look back for exposure
Other options describe possible features but aren't fundamental differences.

questions.questionText: Naturally acquired active immunity would be most likely acquired through which of the following processes?
questions.explanation:
Naturally acquired active immunity comes from actual infection/exposure to pathogens.
Vaccination = artificial active immunity
Antivenin/colostrum = passive immunity transfer
Natural infection triggers the body's own immune response.

questions.questionText: The number of instances of disease or related attribute in a known population at a given time, without distinction between new and old cases is measured by ______.
questions.explanation:
Prevalence = total cases at a time point
Incidence = new cases over time
Odds ratio = measure of association
Attack rate = special incidence measure during outbreaks.

questions.questionText: Which of the following operating room personnel should face the sterile field during a procedure?
options: Only the surgeon and non-sterile personnel
The scrubbed-in technicians and surgeon only
All personnel, both scrubbed in and non-sterile
questions.explanation:
Only sterile (scrubbed) personnel should face the sterile field to maintain asepsis.
Non-sterile personnel should avoid turning their backs to the field as this can contaminate it.

questions.questionText: One of the following statements is false regarding hematoma and its surgical management in pets?
options: Aural hematoma can be managed surgically under infiltration of local anaesthetic over the surgical field
It can occur everywhere on the body
More common in dogs due to mechanical injury to the ear flaps
Aural hematoma can't only managed surgically
questions.explanation:
Aural hematomas CAN be managed non-surgically (aspiration, steroids).
All other statements are correct about hematomas.

questions.questionText: The chief functions of the inflammatory response include:
options: Bringing immune components to injury via cytokines
Destroy and block invasion of microbes
questions.explanation:
All options are correct functions of inflammation:
1) Recruitment via cytokines
2) Tissue repair
3) Microbial destruction/containment.

questions.questionText: Which of the following does not constitute the epidemiology of infections?
options: Understanding the mode of transmission of infections
Studying maintenance of infections in a population
The study of the source of infection and portal of entry
questions.explanation: All listed items (transmission, maintenance, source/portal) are core aspects of infectious disease epidemiology.

questions.questionText: Why sugar is added to about 45% during condensed milk production?
options: To improve the flavour of the milk
To improve colour of the milk
To increase the shelf life of the milk
To improve solid composition of milk
questions.explanation:
High sugar (45%) creates osmotic pressure that inhibits microbial growth, extending shelf life.
While it affects flavor/color/composition, preservation is the primary purpose.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is not true about tracheotomy in dog?
options: Can be conducted if surgery is conducted on upper respiratory tract
Control the animal in lateral recumbence under infiltration of 2% lidocaine HCl intravenously
It is conducted on middle upper third portion of neck
questions.explanation:
Lidocaine should NOT be given IV for tracheotomy (risk of cardiac effects).
Local infiltration is used, and dogs are typically in sternal recumbency.

questions.questionText: Adrenaline/Epinephrine can be indicated or prescribed for all of the following clinical problems, except:
questions.explanation:
Epinephrine causes vasoconstriction which would worsen hypotension.
It's used for asthma (bronchodilation), anaphylaxis, and as a local vasoconstrictor.

questions.questionText: The application of the principles and knowledge of veterinary medicine for the purpose of law is defined as:-
questions.explanation:
Veterinary jurisprudence is the correct term for legal applications of vet medicine.
Animal welfare is broader, not specifically law-focused.

questions.questionText: A testis from a ram was found smaller than normal. Microscopic examination showed reduction in the number and diameter of tubules. What is your diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Hypoplastic testis shows underdevelopment of tubules.
Hypertrophy = increased size
Necrosis = cell death
Tumors would show abnormal cell growth.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not involved in innate resistance?
questions.explanation:
All listed components are part of innate immunity:
- Acute phase proteins (inflammatory response)
- Complement (protein cascade system)
- Lysozyme (antimicrobial enzyme)
- Interferons (antiviral cytokines)
They all work together in early defense.

questions.questionText: One of the following components should not be included as component of semen extender used for chilling:
questions.explanation:
Cryoprotectants (e.g., glycerol) are for freezing, not chilling extenders.
Chilling extenders need buffers, cold shock preventers (egg yolk), and nutrients.

questions.questionText: What trypanosome species is transmitted in nature by both mechanical and cyclical means?
questions.explanation:
T. vivax uses both:
Cyclical (tsetse fly biological vector)
Mechanical (other biting flies)
T. evansi is purely mechanical
T. congolense is cyclical only.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the best characteristic of fever?
options: It increases the viability of many microbial invaders
It is a type of specific immunity
It increases the rapidity of the host immune responses
It is caused only by endogenous pyrogens
questions.explanation:
Fever enhances immune function (e.g., leukocyte mobility, cytokine production).
It's nonspecific, can be caused by exogenous/endogenous pyrogens, and generally inhibits microbes.

questions.questionText: Atropine sulfate is a common anticholinergic drug used in general anesthesia as component of balanced anesthesia, which one explains the drawback of using this drug?
questions.explanation:
Atropine causes blurred vision (not sharpness) via pupil dilation.
Other options are expected anticholinergic effects (not necessarily drawbacks).

questions.questionText: First generation cephalosporins are effective against:-
questions.explanation:
1st gen cephalosporins have best activity against Gram+ aerobes (e.g., Staphylococci).
Poor against anaerobes, Mycobacteria, and limited Gram- coverage.

questions.questionText: When an infection spreads among individual animals, which of the following epidemics occurs?
questions.explanation:
Propagated epidemic = person-to-person/animal-to-animal spread.
Point = single exposure event
Mixed = combination.

questions.questionText: The result above indicates hemoglobinuria, what further laboratory technique will you employ to confirm the underlying cause?
questions.explanation:
Babesia causes intravascular hemolysis → hemoglobinuria.
Giemsa stains blood parasites.
Other options wouldn't identify hemolytic causes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is false about the source of infectious agents?
options: Primary source is a source where the agents have a chance to multiply
Water trough can be contaminated by poultry droppings
Materials of animal origin can act as a primary source
Human can be a primary source for zoonotic diseases
questions.explanation:
Primary source = where agent lives/multiplies (reservoir).
Secondary source = contaminated objects (like water troughs).
Humans can be reservoirs for zoonoses (e.g., rabies).

questions.questionText: You are a qualified and experienced veterinarian running a licensed veterinary clinic. A court may order you to provide professional testimony for the following reasons except:
options: If there is a legal issue that requires determination the price of an animal
If there is a legal issue that requires determination of the cause of death of an animal
If there is a legal issue that requires determination of the health status of an animal
If there is a legal issue that requires determination of the cause and extent of injury inflicted on an animal
questions.explanation:
Vets testify on medical issues (cause of death, injuries, health) not monetary valuation.
Pricing would require appraisal expertise.

questions.questionText: One of the following parasites produces egg which has a spine.
questions.explanation:
Schistosoma eggs have characteristic spines (lateral or terminal).
Fasciola/Taenia/Dicrocoelium eggs lack spines.

questions.questionText: Why is not important in detection of helminth eggs using simple fecal floatation technique?
questions.explanation:
McMaster chamber is for quantitative counts, not simple qualitative floatation.
Basic floatation needs tube, slide, and coverslip.

questions.questionText: Which one is the correct order in tissue processing for histopathological examination?
questions.explanation:
Standard histopathology workflow:
1) Fixation (preserve tissue)
2) Embedding (in paraffin)
3) Sectioning (thin slices)
4) Staining

questions.questionText: Which parasite is responsible to cause a condition known as pruritis ani or perineal irritation in horses?
questions.explanation:
Oxyuris equi (pinworm) causes perianal itching when females lay eggs.
Others are blood/bowel parasites not associated with perineal irritation.

questions.questionText: What is not an example of granulomatous enteritis?
questions.explanation:
Gastric ulcers are erosive, not granulomatous.
Others (TB, Johne's, coligranuloma) cause granulomatous intestinal inflammation.

questions.questionText: No sheep were presented to a veterinary clinic at Fiche. The owner complained the animals have lost body weight, had swelling under the lower jaw. In the last two months, the sheep have been grazing in marshy areas. Up on clinical examination, a swelling under the jaw had soft consistency (watery content), the mucus membranes were pale and their rectal temperature was 37 and 39°C. What could be the most likely disease?
questions.explanation:
Key signs point to fasciolosis (liver fluke):
- Bottle jaw (submandibular edema)
- Anemia (pale mm)
- Grazing marshy areas (snail habitat)
- Weight loss
Paramphistomiasis causes diarrhea, trypanosomosis causes fever.

questions.questionText: The most common source for point epidemic is:-
options: Exposure of a large number of animals to a new but favourable environment
Exposure occurs among individuals in the population
Exposure of animals to an infectious agent within long periods of time
questions.explanation:
Point epidemics result from simultaneous exposure to a common source (e.g., toxic feed).
Propagated epidemics spread gradually.

questions.questionText: One of the following Trypanosome species passes its entire tsetse cycle in the proboscis of tsetse flies:
questions.explanation:
T. congolense develops only in tsetse proboscis (anterior station).
T. brucei migrates to salivary glands
T. vivax develops in proboscis but can also use mechanical transmission.

questions.questionText: Identify the one which is different?
questions.explanation:
Mast cells are granulocytes involved in allergic/inflammatory responses.
The others (NK cells, cytotoxic cells, neutrophils) are primarily involved in cell-mediated cytotoxicity and pathogen destruction.
Mast cells have unique functions in immediate hypersensitivity and tissue repair.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not characteristic of Ketamine anesthesia?
questions.explanation:
Ketamine causes muscle rigidity (not relaxation), tachycardia, and increased respiration.
Muscle relaxation requires additional agents.

questions.questionText: All of the following forms of hernia do have sac except?
questions.explanation:
Diaphragmatic hernias lack true sacs (organs protrude through diaphragm).
Others (inguinal, scrotal, ventrolateral) typically have peritoneal sacs.

questions.questionText: One of the following techniques does not help in preserving fecal samples.
questions.explanation:
Normal saline doesn't preserve feces (just maintains osmolarity).
Alcohol/formalin fix, refrigeration slows degradation.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a lung worm of small ruminants:
questions.explanation:
D. viviparous is a cattle lungworm.
Others infect small ruminants:
M. capillaris, P. rufescens (small lungworms)
D. filaria (large lungworm of sheep/goats).

questions.questionText: One of the following is not considered as an advantage of applications embryo technologies:
options: Easy to apply in resource limited setting
questions.explanation:
Embryo tech (ET, IVF) requires significant resources (equipment, expertise).
Other options are valid advantages where resources exist.

questions.questionText: The proportion of died animals from the diseased population is called as:-
questions.explanation:
Case fatality rate = deaths among cases.
Morbidity = disease incidence
Prevalence = total cases
Death rate = deaths in whole population.

questions.questionText: A healthy functioning immune system is responsible for all of the following except one:
options: Creation of physical barriers to deter the invasion of microbes
questions.explanation:
Physical barriers (skin, mucus) are innate defenses but not immune system functions.
Immune system handles surveillance, recognition, response.

questions.questionText: It is a nematode with coiled male tail; eggs are lemon shaped with a conspicuous plug at both ends and yellow or brown color. This characteristics belongs to:
questions.explanation:
Trichuris (whipworm) has:
- Coiled male tail
- Bipolar-plugged eggs
Others:
Haemonchus - strongyle eggs
Ascaris - round, thick-shelled
Ancylostoma - thin-shelled oval.

questions.questionText: What of the following is the simplest method for detection of nematode eggs in feces?
questions.explanation:
Direct smear is simplest (feces + saline on slide).
Floatation/sedimentation concentrate eggs
Baermann detects larvae.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a predisposing determinant of disease?
questions.explanation:
Microorganisms are direct causes (not predisposing factors).
Age/sex/occupation predispose by affecting exposure or susceptibility.

questions.questionText: Which of the following drugs is effective against immature and adult fasciola species?
questions.explanation:
Triclabendazole is flukicide effective against all Fasciola stages.
Others:
Albendazole - mainly adults
Closantel - adults
Tetramisole - nematodes only.

questions.questionText: If a relative neutrophil count in a dog is 70% and if the total leukocyte count is 10,000/µL, the absolute count of neutrophils is:-
questions.explanation:
Absolute count = % × total WBC
70% of 10,000 = 7,000/µL neutrophils.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about B-lymphocytes?
options: They are derived from the thymus
They matures in the thymus gland in all birds and mammals
When activated they will divide and form specialized plasma cells which produce antibodies
questions.explanation:
B cells mature in bone marrow/bursa (not thymus, which is for T cells).
Activated B cells become antibody-producing plasma cells.

questions.questionText: Specific immunity exhibit four characteristic attributes which are mediated by lymphocytes. Which of the following is not among the attributes of specific immunity?
questions.explanation:
All are attributes:
Specificity - recognizes particular antigens
Adaptability - diverse responses
Memory - faster secondary response.

questions.questionText: Which condition best describes the causes of alimentary tract haemorrhage?
questions.explanation:
Gastric/abomasal ulcers are the most common cause of significant GI hemorrhage.
Rumen lesions rarely cause hemorrhage due to its stratified squamous epithelium.
Enteritis and parasites can cause blood loss but usually less acute than ulcers.
Ulcers can rapidly lead to severe hemorrhage requiring immediate intervention.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an endectocide?
questions.explanation:
Ivermectin treats endo- and ectoparasites (endectocide).
Others are only anthelmintics (internal parasites).

questions.questionText: Parasitic cirrhosis is caused by:
questions.explanation:
Chronic Fasciola infection causes biliary fibrosis/cirrhosis.
Others don't typically cause cirrhosis:
Haemonchus - anemia
Paramphistomum - rumen
Ascaris - intestinal.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not risk factor for colic in horses?
options: Those associated with feeding practices and management
questions.explanation:
Proper parasite control REDUCES colic risk.
Other options are known risk factors (diet changes, age, prior colic).

questions.questionText: Differentiation of hard ticks from soft ticks is best achieved by:-
options: Number and strength of their legs
questions.explanation:
Hard ticks (Ixodidae) have a dorsal scutum.
Soft ticks (Argasidae) lack this shield.
Other features overlap between groups.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not correct regarding host defenses?
options: First line of defense blocks portals of entry
Non-specific defense includes inflammation and phagocytosis
questions.explanation:
All statements are correct about host defenses:
1) Physical barriers
2) Innate immunity (phagocytes)
3) Adaptive immunity (B/T cells).

questions.questionText: When do the odds ratio and relative risk become the same?
options: When the disease's prevalence is low (less than 5%)
If the outcome of interest is high
The odds ratio and relative risk have no relationship
When the prevalence of the disease exceeds its incidence
questions.explanation:
OR≈RR when disease is rare (<10%).
At higher prevalence, OR overestimates RR.

questions.questionText: Which one is identified as incorrect matching?
options: Palatitis is inflammation of the teeth
Stomatitis is inflammation of the oral mucosa
Glossitis is inflammation of the tongue
Gingivitis inflammation of the mucosa of the glottis
questions.explanation:
Gingivitis = gum inflammation (not glottis).
Palatitis isn't a standard term (pulpitis affects teeth).

questions.questionText: The junction of two ecosystems is referred to as:-
questions.explanation:
Ecotone/ecological interface = transition zone between ecosystems.
Biocenosis = community
Biotype = habitat type.

questions.questionText: The average concentration of hemoglobin within erythrocytes are evaluated by:
questions.explanation:
MCHC = Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin Concentration
Measures Hb concentration per RBC volume.
PCV/HCT = packed cell volume
MCV = cell size.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a differential diagnosis for colic?
questions.explanation:
Glossitis (tongue inflammation) doesn't cause colic signs.
Others can present similarly to GI colic.

questions.questionText: What one of the following is a prerequisite for clinical diagnosis?
options: Knowledge of etiology, clinical signs, and pathogenesis of the diseases
Knowledge of animal immediate surroundings and environments
Basic knowledge of anatomy, physiology, pathology, and disease epidemiology
questions.explanation: All options are important, but anatomy/physiology/pathology form the foundation for interpreting clinical signs.

questions.questionText: Traumatic reticultis associates with one of the following
questions.explanation:
Hardware disease can lead to:
1) Pericarditis (wire penetrates heart)
2) Peritonitis
But pericarditis is classic sequel.

questions.questionText: Traumatic reticultitis associates with one of the following
questions.explanation:
Traumatic reticulitis can lead to pericarditis when sharp objects penetrate the reticulum and diaphragm.
This is called traumatic pericarditis or 'hardware disease'.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is incorrect?
options: Control refers to all measures intended to interfere the occurrence of a disease
Treating diseased animals can reduce disease prevalence
Reduction of morbidity and mortality from a disease can be achieved by control measures
questions.explanation:
All statements are correct about disease control:
1. Definition of control
2. Treatment reduces prevalence
3. Control reduces morbidity/mortality

questions.questionText: Which activities are typical manifestations of severe abdominal pain in horses?
options: Pawing and kicking at the belly
Getting up and lying down repeatedly
questions.explanation:
All options can indicate pain, but looking at flanks and rolling are most characteristic of severe abdominal pain in horses.
The progression typically goes from mild (pawing, looking at flanks) to severe (rolling, lying on back).
Rolling is particularly concerning as it can lead to intestinal torsion.

questions.questionText: Identify the parasite that has Coenurus cerebralis as its larval stage
questions.explanation:
Taenia multiceps → Coenurus cerebralis (causes gid in sheep)
T. solium → Cysticercus cellulosae
T. saginata → C. bovis

questions.questionText: One isn't included in the Clinical signs of lungworm infections in cattle
questions.explanation:
Salivation isn't typical of lungworm (Dictyocaulus).
Classic signs: cough, dyspnea, tachypnea ('husk')

questions.questionText: After a viral infection, humans and animals produce a heterogeneous group of glycoproteins named as:-
questions.explanation:
Interferons = antiviral glycoproteins
Triggered by viral infection
Part of innate immunity

questions.questionText: Which of the following animals is a maintenance host for African Horse Sickness and Foot and Mouth Disease, respectively?
questions.explanation:
Zebra = AHS reservoir
African buffalo = FMD reservoir
Note: Birds don't maintain these viruses

questions.questionText: Which parasite is responsible to cause a condition known as pruritis ani or perineal irritation in horses?
questions.explanation:
Oxyuris equi (pinworm) causes perineal itching
Eggs are laid around anus → intense irritation

questions.questionText: What is not an example of granulomatous enteritis?
questions.explanation:
Gastric ulcers = erosive, not granulomatous
Others:
- Coligranuloma (E. coli)
- TB (mycobacterial)
- Johne's (paratuberculosis)

questions.questionText: The most common source for point epidemic is:-
options: Exposure of a large number of animals to a new but favourable environment
Exposure occurs among individuals in the population
Exposure of animals to an infectious agent within long periods of time
questions.explanation:
Point epidemic = simultaneous exposure to common source (e.g., toxins)
Distinct from propagated epidemics (person-to-person)

questions.questionText: The picture below was taken from a bone marrow aspiration stained with Giemsa. The large pink stained cells are white blood cells. The animal may be suffering from
questions.explanation:
Excessive WBCs in marrow suggest leukemia
Thrombocytopenia = low platelets
Erythrocytopenia = low RBCs

questions.questionText: One of the following Trypanosome species passes its entire tsetse cycle in the proboscis of tsetse flies:
questions.explanation:
T. congolense = proboscis only
T. vivax = proboscis + anterior station
T. brucei = salivary glands

questions.questionText: Identify the one which is different?
questions.explanation:
Mast cells = granulocytes (allergy)
Others are involved in cellular immunity/viral defense

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not characteristic of Ketamine anaesthesia?
questions.explanation:
Ketamine causes:
- Catalepsy (rigid muscles)
- Sympathetic stimulation (↑HR)
- Minimal respiratory depression

questions.questionText: All of the following forms of hernia do have sac except?
questions.explanation:
Diaphragmatic hernia = no true sac (organ displacement)
Others have peritoneal sacs

questions.questionText: One of the following techniques does not help in preserving fecal samples.
questions.explanation:
NaCl solution = flotation medium (not preservative)
Preservatives: formalin, alcohol, refrigeration

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a lung worm of small ruminants:
questions.explanation:
D. viviparus = cattle lungworm
Others affect sheep/goats:
- Muellerius (most common)
- Protostrongylus
- D. filaria

questions.questionText: One of the following is not considered as an advantage of applications embryo technologies
options: Easy to apply in resource limited setting
questions.explanation:
Embryo tech (ET, IVF) requires:
- Advanced labs
- Skilled personnel
- Expensive equipment

questions.questionText: The proportion of died animals from the diseased population is called as:-
questions.explanation:
CFR = deaths/diseased animals
Mortality rate = deaths/total population

questions.questionText: A healthy functioning immune system is responsible for all of the following except one:
options: Creation of physical barriers to deter the invasion of microbes
questions.explanation:
Physical barriers (skin, mucus) are innate but not immune functions
Immune system = recognition/response

questions.questionText: Which term describes when a disease is constantly present in a population at low levels?
questions.explanation:
Endemic = constant baseline presence
Epidemic = sudden increase
Pandemic = worldwide spread

questions.questionText: One of the following characterizes the practice of increased antibiotic consumption
options: Creates selection pressure for resistant strains to propagate
questions.explanation:
Antibiotic overuse → selects resistant strains
Doesn't cause mutations but favors existing resistant bacteria

questions.questionText: It is a nematode with coiled male tail; eggs are lemon shaped with a conspicuous plug at both ends and yellow or brown color. This characteristics belongs to:
questions.explanation:
Trichuris (whipworm) characteristics:
- Coiled male tail
- Bipolar-plugged eggs
Causes diarrhea in dogs/livestock

questions.questionText: What of the following is the simplest method for detection of nematode eggs in feces?
questions.explanation:
Direct smear = quickest but least sensitive
Floatation (sucrose/salt) = more sensitive for light eggs
Baermann = larvae

questions.questionText: Which type of anemia is characterized by the bone marrow's inability to produce RBCs?
questions.explanation:
Generative = non-regenerative (marrow failure)
Others involve RBC loss/destruction with marrow response

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a predisposing determinant of disease?
questions.explanation:
Microorganism = causative agent (not predisposing factor)
Predisposing factors = host/environment traits increasing susceptibility

questions.questionText: Which of the following drugs is effective against immature and adult Fasciola species?
questions.explanation:
Triclabendazole = gold standard for all Fasciola stages
Others lack efficacy against early immature flukes

questions.questionText: If a relative neutrophil count in a dog is 70% and if the total leukocyte count is 10,000/µL, the absolute count of neutrophils is:-
questions.explanation:
Calculation: 70% of 10,000 = 7,000 cells/µL
Absolute count > relative % is clinically significant

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about B-lymphocytes?
options: They are derived from the thymus
They matures in the thymus gland in all birds and mammals
When activated they will divide and form specialized plasma cells which produce antibodies
questions.explanation:
B-cells → plasma cells → antibodies
Mature in bone marrow (not thymus, which is for T-cells)

questions.questionText: Specific immunity exhibit four characteristic attributes which are mediated by lymphocytes. Which of the following is not among the attributes of specific immunity?
questions.explanation:
All are key attributes:
1. Specificity (antigen recognition)
2. Adaptability (diverse responses)
3. Memory (secondary responses)

questions.questionText: Alternatively, if the result of the first test indicates hematuria, what additional test can you do on the urine?
questions.explanation:
Hematuria confirmation requires RBC identification
Sediment exam differentiates true hematuria vs hemoglobinuria

questions.questionText: Which condition best describes the causes of alimentary tract haemorrhage?
questions.explanation:
Blood-sucking worms (Haemonchus) cause anemia, not frank hemorrhage
Ulcers/enteritis can cause GI bleeding

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an endectocide?
questions.explanation:
Ivermectin = endectocide (internal + external parasites)
Others are narrow-spectrum anthelmintics

questions.questionText: Parasitic cirrhosis is caused by:
questions.explanation:
Chronic Fasciola → liver fibrosis/cirrhosis
Others don't typically cause cirrhosis:
Haemonchus → anemia
Paramphistomes → rumen

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not risk factor for colic in horses?
options: Those associated with feeding practices and management
questions.explanation:
Proper parasite control REDUCES colic risk
Others are known risk factors:
- Sudden feed changes (management)
- Age/breed (extrinsic)
- Previous colic (medical history)
